description: Manually declared expected outcomes, independent of both implementations. Events that are disabled produce -1; the next attempted event starts from the last accepted state. Configurations and states use the wire contract in README.md.

scenarios.name: beforeAppointment
scenarios.claim: Execution, revocation, notice, and withdrawal require their prerequisites; stuttering does not.

scenarios.name: jointSoloARejected
scenarios.claim: A joint mandate does not authorize A to execute alone.

scenarios.name: jointSoloBRejected
scenarios.claim: The joint requirement applies symmetrically to B.

scenarios.name: jointExecution
scenarios.claim: Both authorized agents may jointly execute the scoped act.

scenarios.name: independentA
scenarios.claim: Explicit independent permission allows A to execute alone.

scenarios.name: independentB
scenarios.claim: Explicit independent permission allows B to execute alone.

scenarios.name: independentJoint
scenarios.claim: Independent permission does not prevent joint execution.

scenarios.name: immediateRevocationBeforeNotice
scenarios.claim: In the immediate profile, revocation blocks joint execution before either agent knows.

scenarios.name: immediateIndependentRevocation
scenarios.claim: In the immediate profile, lack of notice does not preserve either solo authority.

scenarios.name: knowledgeJointBeforeNotice
scenarios.claim: The alternative knowledge profile retains both authorities before notice.

scenarios.name: knowledgeIndependentBeforeNotice
scenarios.claim: The alternative knowledge profile retains independent authority before notice.

scenarios.name: noticeABreaksJoint
scenarios.claim: Notice to A prevents a later joint act in the knowledge profile.

scenarios.name: noticeBBreaksJoint
scenarios.claim: Notice to B prevents a later joint act in the knowledge profile.

scenarios.name: asymmetricNoticeA
scenarios.claim: Notice to A does not become knowledge of B; B's independent authority remains.

scenarios.name: asymmetricNoticeB
scenarios.claim: Notice to B does not become knowledge of A; A's independent authority remains.

scenarios.name: bothKnow
scenarios.claim: After both agents know of revocation, neither solo nor joint execution is authorized.

scenarios.name: withdrawalABreaksJoint
scenarios.claim: A's withdrawal prevents joint execution without granting B solo permission.

scenarios.name: withdrawalBBreaksJoint
scenarios.claim: B's withdrawal prevents joint execution without granting A solo permission.

scenarios.name: withdrawalIndependentA
scenarios.claim: A's withdrawal blocks A but leaves an independently authorized B able to execute.

scenarios.name: withdrawalIndependentB
scenarios.claim: B's withdrawal blocks B but leaves an independently authorized A able to execute.

scenarios.name: outsideScopeRejected
scenarios.claim: Independent permission changes the participants requirement, not the scope of the grant.

scenarios.name: acceptedHistoryPersists
scenarios.claim: Later revocation, notice, and withdrawals do not erase an already accepted execution.

scenarios.name: oneModeledExecution
scenarios.claim: The pilot admits only one recorded execution, not repeated acts under the same grant.

scenarios.name: noRepeatedLifecycleEvents
scenarios.claim: Appointment, revocation, each notice, and each withdrawal are one-time events in this abstraction.

scenarios.name: noticeRequiresRevocation
scenarios.claim: The modeled notice is notice of an actual revocation; earlier notice attempts are disabled.

scenarios.name: withdrawalDespiteAbsentNotice
scenarios.claim: An agent's own withdrawal blocks execution even if that agent has not learned of revocation.
